method: Sequential matched baseline and candidate. Three fresh implicit wallets per arm. Same custody versions. One SDK and harness serve both arms. Only the Gateway session commit/readback batch differs. Only the NEAR signer is loaded. First signature is an independently verified NEP-413 message without account funding.
scope: Existing staging testnet resources. No new infrastructure or package release.
changes: Append the exact session readback to the existing six-statement direct-issuance transaction.
Share the mint query and row parser between ordinary reads and batched commit readback.
Preserve transactional active authority and method checks, identity and credential checks, quota/session change parity, and replay behavior.

outcome: No finalization speedup established: median 2649.368ms to 2661.267ms (+11.899ms, 0.45%). The internal side-effect span was 1647ms to 1640ms. Overall registration-to-verified-message median decreased by 811.274ms while unchanged Yao code also ran faster. Retain one transactional session readback and one fewer D1 call without claiming a measured latency gain.
limitations: Three sequential samples per arm establish neither percentiles nor a maximum guarantee.
Authenticated Yao and wallet-commit metrics sum corresponding HTTP durations per sample, never stage medians.
Browser registration-to-signature time includes automation and UI settlement. Fresh wallets do not prove cold Workers or DOs.
Gateway-wide D1 and backend Console call counts remain unknown. Application timers omit some CPU work.
Existing APAC home hints remain. Actual physical colocation was not remeasured.
